lesson_title: Factorising Trinomials: Read the Signs First
hook_text: Stop guessing factor pairs. The signs tell you the answer's shape before you hunt.
clip_script: Before listing a single factor pair, read the signs like a detective. The product is negative, so the two numbers carry opposite signs. The sum is negative, so the larger number, in size, wears the minus. Two deductions made before any hunting. Now the factor pairs of sixty: one and sixty — fifty-nine. Two and thirty — twenty-eight. Five and twelve — seven. Six and ten — four. Found it. The pair is negative ten and positive six. Verify both conditions: negative ten times six is negative sixty. Negative ten plus six is negative four. Both keys turn; the lock is open.
visual_style: A detective's corkboard: two sign-clues pinned first, then a ladder of factor pairs crossed out rung by rung until 6 and 10 light up and the padlock springs open.
pacing: Two quick clue beats, rhythmic elimination down the ladder, double-check landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and split the middle term of 4x² − 4x − 15 yourself.
